risks.name: Unauthorized wire transfer
risks.description: Impersonated customer instructions could result in a payment to an unauthorized beneficiary.

inherent.likelihoodRationale: Wire instructions can be impersonated across standard and urgent requests. The new exception route increases the opportunity for manual intervention.
inherent.impactRationale: An unauthorized payment could cause material financial loss and disrupt customer operations.

residual.likelihoodRationale: Current testing supports the standard route only. The urgent route and shared contact source limit the protection that can presently be established.
residual.impactRationale: Existing controls do not materially limit the size of a payment if an unauthorized instruction succeeds.

risks.name: Incorrect payment details
risks.description: Incorrect beneficiary or amount details could result in a misdirected payment.

inherent.likelihoodRationale: Manual entry creates a possibility of incorrect beneficiary or amount details.
inherent.impactRationale: Errors could require recovery activity and cause significant customer disruption.

residual.likelihoodRationale: The documented detail check is supported by current standard-route testing with no exceptions in the sample.
residual.impactRationale: A payment error can still require recovery and customer remediation even when detected promptly.

risks.name: Delayed execution
risks.description: Queue or verification delays could cause a payment to miss the processing cutoff.

inherent.likelihoodRationale: Processing peaks and verification delays can affect the payment queue.
inherent.impactRationale: A missed cutoff could delay settlement and disrupt the customer's obligations.

residual.likelihoodRationale: Queue monitoring and escalation are supported by the October service review.
residual.impactRationale: Escalation reduces delay likelihood but cannot eliminate the impact of a missed settlement.

controls.name: Callback verification
controls.design: A callback to the registered customer contact verifies the request before release. The urgent-route exception requires supervisory approval.
controls.operation: Not established for the urgent route
controls.evidence: 25 standard-wire samples. No exceptions in the tested population.
controls.designConclusion: Documented design; urgent-route coverage needs review.

controls.name: Supervisory approval
controls.design: A separate supervisor reviews the instruction and confirmation against the customer-contact record before authorizing release.
controls.operation: Not established for the urgent route
controls.evidence: The latest test predates the urgent exception route and does not establish its performance.
controls.designConclusion: Separate approval is documented; an independent information source is not established.

controls.name: Payment detail check
controls.design: A second operator compares entered beneficiary and amount against the verified instruction.
controls.evidence: 25 payment-detail samples reviewed in October; no exceptions identified.
controls.designConclusion: The documented design addresses this risk.

controls.name: Cutoff monitoring
controls.design: The queue is monitored before cutoff; delayed items are escalated to the duty supervisor.
controls.evidence: October queue records show timely escalation for the sampled processing days.
controls.designConclusion: The documented design addresses this risk.

controls.name: Customer payment confirmation
controls.purpose: Confirm beneficiary and amount before release
controls.design: The customer confirms beneficiary and amount through the authenticated payment channel before a standard wire is released. This supplements the operator entry check; it does not by itself establish independent identity verification for an urgent request.
controls.operation: Standard-route confirmations observed in the sample
controls.evidence: 25 standard-wire customer confirmations were reviewed in October. No beneficiary or amount discrepancies were found in that sample. Urgent-route requests were not tested.
controls.mappingHint: Adds customer confirmation to the operator detail check. Assess any shared instruction source and the limits of standard-route testing.

sources.title: Prior assessment
sources.scope: Wire-transfer assessment before the urgent-route change
sources.excerpt: Residual unauthorized-wire risk was assessed as Moderate (8), based on likelihood 2 and impact 4. The standard route used callback verification and separate supervisory approval.

sources.title: Revised wire procedure
sources.scope: Standard wires and the newly introduced urgent exception route
sources.excerpt: Standard requests follow the required verification and dual-approval sequence. Urgent requests may use the exception route with supervisory approval. The reviewer consults the registered customer-contact record.

sources.title: Callback procedure
sources.excerpt: Verify using the registered customer contact.

sources.title: Approval checklist
sources.excerpt: Compare confirmation against the customer-contact record.

sources.title: Standard-wire control test
sources.scope: 25 standard-wire samples; urgent exception route not in scope
sources.excerpt: 25 standard-wire samples were reviewed. No exceptions were identified in the tested population. Testing was completed before the urgent exception route was introduced on October 5, 2026.

sources.title: Intercepted fraud attempt
sources.scope: One intercepted urgent request; no payment loss
sources.excerpt: An urgent request involved recently amended customer-contact details. A secondary check intercepted the instruction before release. The event does not establish that every control failed; the relationship between the change and the attempted fraud requires assessment.

sources.title: Payment detail testing
sources.excerpt: The sampled detail checks compared beneficiary and amount with the verified instructions. No exceptions were identified in the 25 sampled items. Results support only the documented population and period.

sources.title: Queue service review
sources.scope: October cutoff monitoring and escalation samples
sources.excerpt: Queue records for the sampled days showed monitoring before cutoff and escalation of delayed requests to the duty supervisor. The review does not establish the availability of every verification service under all scenarios.

sources.title: Customer confirmation review
sources.scope: 25 standard-wire beneficiary and amount confirmations; urgent requests excluded
sources.excerpt: The sampled standard-wire requests included customer confirmation of beneficiary and amount in the authenticated payment channel before release. No detail discrepancies were found in the 25 sampled confirmations. The review does not establish urgent-route effectiveness or independent identity verification.

action.title: Test urgent-wire verification and contact changes
action.evidence: Document the test population, exceptions, and the independent source used for verification.

challenge: How will targeted testing cover urgent wires after contact changes, and how will interim verification avoid the same shared source?

responses.initial: Staff have been reminded of the callback procedure.
responses.revised: Include post-change urgent requests and recently amended contact records. Record exception samples and document the independent source used for verification. Closure evidence will include test results, exceptions, and proof of that verification source.
